stem: In the formula $I=\dfrac{bh^2}{12}$, $b={=b}$ and $I={=I}$. Mark on the number line every value of $h$ that makes the formula true.
solution: Put the two given numbers into $I=\dfrac{bh^2}{12}$, so that $h$ is the only letter left.
Do the same to both sides to undo what is joined to $h^2$: multiply by 12, then divide by the number that multiplies $h^2$, until $h^2$ stands alone and equals a positive number.
Ask which numbers square to that value. Taking the square root of both sides gives two answers, the positive root and its negative, because a negative number squared is also positive.
Tap the positive root on the number line, then tap the negative root: two points the same distance from 0, one on each side.
notes: Numeric-substitution instances of objective 3 only; the symbolic rearrangement (r = ±√(V/(πh))) is NOT exercised and is a gap. The anchor's own numbers (I=384, b=18, h=±16) are unreachable: range may be at most 24 wide (FR-1207), so the rows are scaled to roots of 3 to 8. Graded as a SET, so the stem says what is asked (every value that makes the formula true) and any order of tapping is correct (FR-1205). Not mapped: extra-values (no listed misconception names it; a stray extra point has no single dominant cause) and sign-flipped (the target set is symmetric, so a negated set is the correct set and it cannot fire). missed-values also fires if the student marked only the NEGATIVE root; the feedback text should therefore say 'there is a second value' without assuming which one was marked. Targets are given as a whole-array placeholder ('{=t}') so only a typed whole-value substitution is needed; if the substituter is scalar-only, emit each row as a literal spec instead.
